Upper Serangoon

Upper Serangoon

Upper Serangoon 99

  1. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Ah Hock Fried Hokkien Mee

    A Michelin Plate stall and Chomp Chomp's most famous name — thick yellow noodles and bee hoon fried with prawns and squid in a prawn stock simmered for hours, finished with a dollop of sambal. The go-to plate at Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Daniel Food Diary, HungryGoWhere, Seth Lui

  2. Must see · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Ming Fa Duck Rice

    One of Singapore's best Teochew braised duck rice stalls, tucked in Hougang's Hainanese Village Centre (Lorong Ah Soo). Tender lean duck over yam rice, drenched in a mildly sweet-savoury five-spice sauce, with an anchovy-loaded sambal. Opens at dawn and usually sells out by early lunch.

    Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-01, Singapore 530105

    Recommended by Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  3. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Hougang Oyster Omelette & Fried Kway Teow

    A 30-year Hougang heritage stall run by Mr and Mrs Ong that still fries its oyster omelette in pork lard, with big juicy oysters and a fragrant char kway teow alongside. One of the island's best-rated orh luak, worth the queue.

    Blk 435A Hougang Avenue 8, Singapore 531435

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  4. Must see · Upper Serangoon

    Hougang Tou Mu Kung (Kew Ong Yah Temple)

    Singapore's oldest temple dedicated to the Nine Emperor Gods (Kew Ong Yah), completed 1921 and gazetted a National Monument on 14 Jan 2005. Its blend of Hokkien and later Teochew roof forms anchors Hougang's Teochew heritage, and it remains the focus of the annual Nine Emperor Gods Festival.

    Look for Free entry; busiest during the ninth-lunar-month festival

    779A Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia, National Library Board

  5. Must see · Upper Serangoon

    Kampong Lorong Buangkok

    Singapore's last surviving mainland village, established in 1956 when traditional-medicine seller Sng Teow Koon bought the swampy land and rented plots to Malay and Chinese families. A cluster of zinc-roofed houses on dirt tracks around a surau, in the Trafalgar (Buangkok) subzone of Hougang; Ms Sng Mui Hong, the founder's youngest daughter, still lives here as landlord. Old four-digit street signs survive.

    Look for Free; a living village — visit respectfully, don't enter homes

    7 Lorong Buangkok (off Gerald Drive, via Buangkok Crescent), Singapore 547557

    Recommended by National Library Board, TheSmartLocal, Wikipedia

  6. Must see · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Chomp Chomp Satay

    One of two Chomp Chomp stalls listed in the MICHELIN Guide with a Michelin Plate — skewers grilled over charcoal to order, a supper-time institution best eaten late at Serangoon Gardens with a plate of BBQ chicken wings alongside.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Daniel Food Diary, HungryGoWhere

  7. Must see · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Aliff Nasi Lemak

    The most-recommended stall in the market — a Muslim-owned nasi lemak (from S$3) built on freshly squeezed coconut milk, pandan-scented rice and a shiok sambal, with crisp ikan bilis and add-ons. Serangoon Gardens' daytime counterpoint to Chomp Chomp.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  8. Must see · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Original Simon Road Hokkien Mee

    Third- and fourth-generation hawkers who have fried their wet-style Hokkien mee to the same recipe since 1960 — whole prawns, squid rings and pork belly over noodles and bee hoon fried dry so they drink up a prawn-head-and-pork-rib stock, with free-flow crispy lard. Named for its old Simon Road home, now relocated to Kovan 209.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, #01-66, Singapore 530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg

  9. Must see · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Anshun Seafood Soup

    Widely cited as Singapore's best-rated fish soup — a clean, refined broth from a couple who started at Zion Road Blk 91 in 2002 before landing under a quiet Hougang coffeeshop. The 'hei bai' bowl of fried and sliced fish together, done with milk, is the order.

    174C Hougang Avenue 1, Singapore 533174

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  10. Must see · Upper Serangoon

    Church of the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary

    A National Monument (gazetted 14 Jan 2005) and the historic heart of Serangoon's Teochew Catholic community, which was mostly farmers in the 19th century. The present Gothic church — pointed arches, a soaring nave — was blessed on 8 Dec 1901 and restored in 2019; the mission dates to pioneer priest Fr Ambrose Maistre in 1852.

    Look for Free entry; a stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail

    1259 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534795

    Recommended by National Library Board, Wikipedia

  11. Must see · Upper Serangoon

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre

    Serangoon Gardens' legendary supper hawker centre, open since 1972 with around 36 stalls. A night-time institution for BBQ stingray and sotong, Hokkien mee, satay, satay bee hoon, orh luak and charcoal chicken wings — as much a neighbourhood landmark as an eating spot.

    Look for Evenings to late night; busiest for supper

    20 Kensington Park Road, Singapore 557269

    Recommended by Wikipedia, The Honeycombers

  12. Must see · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang

    A MICHELIN Guide-listed stall that pairs fragrant coconut rice with Ayam Taliwang, the fiery Lombok-style grilled chicken — the smoky, chilli-slicked bird against the cool creamy rice. The Ci Yuan branch of a beloved north-east name, right in Hougang.

    Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-40, Singapore 538776

    Recommended by MICHELIN Guide, Daniel Food Diary

  13. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Sin Heng Kee Porridge

    A Hougang corner-stall congee institution with a perpetual 30-minute queue — thick, hearty bowls of smooth Cantonese-style porridge piled with generous ingredients, warming Hougang residents for decades.

    685 Hougang Street 61, #01-150, S530685

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui

  14. Worth the detour · Upper Serangoon

    Chee Tong Temple

    Completed in 1987 and designed by Tay Kheng Soon of Akitek Tenggara, this is widely regarded as Singapore's first truly modernist Chinese temple — its roof rising in eight-sided prisms that evoke a lotus, its corners deliberately kept un-sharp on the deities' guidance. A Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gem' and a documented modern-movement building.

    Look for Active temple; open daytime

    62 Hougang Avenue 3, Singapore 538844

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Docomomo Singapore, National Library Board

  15. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Chomp Chomp Fried Oyster

    The standout orh luak of Chomp Chomp — eggs and starch fried until charred and crisp at the edges around plump, briny oysters, drizzled with tangy chilli. A perennial pick across the centre's food-guide round-ups.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, HungryGoWhere, Seth Lui

  16. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Good Luck BBQ Chicken Wings

    Chicken wings are practically Chomp Chomp's mascot, and Good Luck (Stall 29) grills some of the most sought-after — burnished, charred-edged skin over juicy meat, at roughly S$1.30 a wing. A supper staple of the Serangoon Gardens crowd.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-29, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  17. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Hai Wei Yuan BBQ

    Chomp Chomp's best sambal BBQ seafood — fresh, flaky stingray blanketed in an addictive sambal and grilled on a banana leaf (from S$12 for a small), plus BBQ sotong and cockles. A late-night favourite that draws its own queue.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by HungryGoWhere, Seth Lui, The Honeycombers

  18. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Ang Sar Lee Satay Bee Hoon

    A 40-plus-year Chomp Chomp veteran plating thin bee hoon drowned in a fragrant satay peanut gravy with cuttlefish, prawns, pork and tau pok — the Serangoon Gardens rendition of a dish few hawkers still make well.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere, The Honeycombers

  19. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Ah Seng Braised Duck Rice

    Rated among Singapore's best Teochew braised duck — tender, herbal braised duck over rice (from S$4) with pig's stomach soup and offal, from a decades-old recipe. Queues form before it opens.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-44, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Eatbook.sg

  20. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Serangoon Garden Bakery & Confectionery

    A 40-year neighbourhood bakery baking from 2am — classic coconut, cream-puff, chicken-sausage and curry buns from S$1.10, all made from scratch. A generational fixture inside the market.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-45/46, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost)

  21. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Fatt Soon Kueh

    A decades-old stall hand-making Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh and gu chye kueh at around S$1 each, using only fresh fillings. A Kovan 209 heritage name.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-17, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey)

  22. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Upper Serangoon

    Hougang Hainanese Curry Rice

    The lunch-hour queue of Kovan 209 — a heaped plate of Hainanese-style chye png flooded with curry, braise and pork gravies, with fried pork chop and cabbage. Old-school comfort food.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Her World Singapore

  23. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Upper Serangoon

    Pow Sing Restaurant

    A Serangoon Gardens institution since 1983 — the Hainanese founders opened a chicken rice stall, then hired a Nonya chef, and today it is rated among Singapore's best traditional Hainanese chicken rice with a Peranakan zi char spread.

    59 Serangoon Garden Way, S555955

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, ladyironchef (Brad Lau), City Nomads (Singapore city guide)

  24. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Apollo Coffee Bar

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary

  25. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Naked Ice Cream

    A late-night Kovan dessert cafe open until 2am, pairing crisp waffles with handcrafted ice cream in offbeat flavours — a viral-friendly stop on the Upper Serangoon supper strip.

    957 Upper Serangoon Road, S534717

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg, ladyironchef (Brad Lau)

  26. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Seng Kee Mushroom Minced Meat Noodle

    A 40-plus-year mushroom minced-meat noodle stall — dry mee pok balanced with a house chilli, deep slow-braised mushroom sauce and crispy pork lard, plus a fish-maw soup its regulars swear by. One of Serangoon Garden Market's most cited names.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-36, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  27. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    East Bistro

    A family-style Cantonese-Teochew restaurant at myVillage helmed by ex-Lei Garden head chef Tony Wong (40-plus years, credited as the original creator of mango sago with pomelo) — hearty zi char and a full dim sum spread.

    myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, #02-01, 1 Maju Avenue, S556679

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg

  28. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Denzy Gelato

    An under-HDB dessert cafe by an Italy-trained gelato-maker who won the Singapore Gelato Championship in 2019 ('Singapore's Best Gelato') with a Pear, Ginger and Ginger Flower scoop inspired by his father's Chinese rojak. The Hougang outlet opened January 2023.

    684 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-953, Singapore 530684

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg

  29. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Apollo Grilled Western Food

    A 30-year hawker Western stall at Hainanese Village Centre — crispy-outside, tender-inside chicken cutlet, chicken chop, pork chop and fish & chips. Old-school flame-grilled plates at hawker prices.

    Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-32, Singapore 530105

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, The Honeycombers

  30. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Jade's Chicken

    A Korean-owned hawker stall at Ci Yuan turning out legit Korean fried chicken — crackly-crisp, in flavours like honey butter — from around S$6.50. Hawker-priced KFC done properly.

    Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-18, Singapore 538776

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  31. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Breakfast Club

    A corner-kopitiam stall two minutes from Kovan MRT doing all-day Western breakfasts — big brekkies, pancakes, creamy scrambled eggs — at hawker prices from S$3.90. Cafe brunch without the cafe markup.

    941 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534709

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary, Mothership

  32. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Hajime Tonkatsu & Ramen

    A tonkatsu specialist at myVillage by Chef Tan, using Sangenton pork air-flown from Japan, each loin tenderised and breaded only on order for a super-crunchy cutlet. Serangoon Gardens' go-to for premium katsu and ramen.

    myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, 1 Maju Avenue, #02-07/8/9, Singapore 556679

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Daniel Food Diary, HungryGoWhere

  33. Worth the detour · Upper Serangoon

    Serangoon Garden Estate & Circus

    One of Singapore's oldest private landed estates, laid out in the 1950s by British developer Steven Charles Macey to house British, Australian and NZ servicemen from the nearby RAF Chia Keng camp — which is why nearly every street bears a British name. The Circus roundabout is its social heart, ringed by Chomp Chomp, the market and myVillage.

    Look for Residential estate; open streetscape

    Serangoon Garden Circus (Serangoon Garden Way / Kensington Park Road), Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Remember Singapore

  34. Worth the detour · Upper Serangoon

    Hougang Heritage Trail

    NHB's self-guided trail through 'Au Kang' — one of Singapore's oldest heartland towns and a historic Teochew enclave. Eighteen sites across three routes ('Landmarks of Hougang', 'Institutions of Service', 'Architectural Gems'), and the first heartland trail to include two National Monuments (Church of the Nativity and Tou Mu Kung).

    Look for Free; booklet & map on Roots.gov.sg

    Upper Serangoon Road (trail markers near Kovan MRT), Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Little Day Out

  35. Worth the detour · Upper Serangoon

    Punggol Park

    A 16-hectare Hougang park built around a 5-hectare lake — a former sand quarry once used to reclaim the area's swamps. Popular for lakeside jogging, fishing decks and a heron-frequented waterfront, and a green anchor of the Hougang edge.

    Look for Open 24h, free

    Hougang Avenue 8 (junction of Hougang Ave 8 & Ave 10), Singapore

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NParks (National Parks Board)

  36. Worth the detour · Upper Serangoon

    Masjid Haji Yusoff

    The oldest mosque in Hougang, built in 1921 on land donated by Gujarati merchant-philanthropist Ahmad Mohamed Salleh Angullia to serve the area's Muslim community of farmers and traders. A stop on the Hougang Heritage Trail, just off Upper Serangoon Road near Kovan.

    Look for Active mosque; visitors welcome outside prayer times

    2 Hillside Drive, Singapore 548920

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  37. Worth the detour · Upper Serangoon

    Lorong Halus Wetland (Serangoon Reservoir)

    An 18-football-field wetland on the Hougang/Defu edge — a former landfill transformed into a natural water-treatment site whose cattails bio-remediate rainwater before it enters the adjoining Serangoon Reservoir. Bounded by Kangkar to the west and Defu Industrial Park to the south, it's a family recreation spot reached over the red steel-railway-style Lorong Halus Bridge from Punggol Promenade.

    Look for Open daily, free; cycling, fishing decks & birdwatching

    Lorong Halus Wetland, Lorong Halus North (eastern bank of Serangoon Reservoir), Singapore

    Recommended by NParks (National Parks Board), PUB, Singapore's National Water Agency

  38. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Garden Street Kway Chap

    A long-running kway chap stall (formerly Blanco Court) ladling silky flat rice sheets in braising liquor with well-stewed Teochew pig offal, braised egg and tau pok — a market breakfast institution.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-21, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  39. Worth the detour · Hainanese Chicken Rice · Upper Serangoon

    Poh Poh Roasted Chicken Rice

    A market favourite for old-school roasted and poached Hainanese chicken rice, repeatedly singled out across the Serangoon Garden Market food-guide round-ups.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  40. Worth the detour · Indian & Roti Prata · Upper Serangoon

    R.K. Eating House

    The 24-hour prata and mamak institution of Serangoon Gardens, famed for crispy plain prata, the over-the-top 'roti tsunami', chocolate prata and maggi mee goreng — its R.K. Special once a Sunday Times 'Cheap & Good' pick.

    1 Kensington Park Road, S557253

    Recommended by Seth Lui, The Honeycombers

  41. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat

    A tiny, wildly popular Kovan streetside zi char serving Teochew-style fish head steamboat in traditional charcoal aluminium pots — pomfret, red grouper or bighead carp — plus salted-egg pork ribs and prawn-paste chicken. Usually packed out by 5.30pm.

    203 Hougang Street 21, #01-89, S530203

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), City Nomads (Singapore city guide)

  42. Worth the detour · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Ponggol Nasi Lemak

    The perennial after-midnight queue on Upper Serangoon Road is a Kovan landmark in itself. Founded 1979 (by the eldest of the Koh nasi lemak family), it's iconic for Chinese-style coconut rice with super-crispy chicken wings, luncheon meat and fried egg.

    965 Upper Serangoon Road, S534721

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, ladyironchef (Brad Lau)

  43. Worth the detour · Thai · Upper Serangoon

    Yaowarat Thai Kway Chap

    A Kovan casual restaurant doing a distinctive Thai take on kway chap — a light, peppery broth (milder than bak kut teh) with silky, curled rice sheets and Thai-style braised sides, open till 3am for the supper crowd.

    945 Upper Serangoon Road, S534711

  44. Worth the detour · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Tom's Palette (Kovan)

    The Kovan branch of homegrown gelateria Tom's Palette, opened March 2024 and open till midnight, known for adventurous flavours and a putu-mayam-topped cone nodding to the area's coconut-plantation past. Honest note: after 21 years, both Tom's Palette outlets are set to close in October 2026.

    Block 212 Hougang Street 21, #01-333, S530212

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  45. Worth the detour · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Lola's Cafe

    A Kovan brunch stalwart a short walk from the MRT and one of the few dog-friendly cafes in the area — hearty brunch plates, truffle linguine and desserts like the oozy goma black-sesame tart and Lola's chocolate cake.

    5 Simon Road, S545893

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, ladyironchef (Brad Lau)

  46. Worth the detour · Thai · Upper Serangoon

    Nakhon Kitchen

    The pioneer of affordable neighbourhood Thai in Kovan (since 2008), the most popular eatery on Hougang Street 21 — a near-constant queue for pandan chicken, green curry, mango salad and pineapple fried rice at hawker prices.

    Block 212 Hougang Street 21, #01-341, S530212

    Recommended by ladyironchef (Brad Lau), HungryGoWhere

  47. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Curry & Curry

    203 Hougang Street 21, #01-45, S530203

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), ladyironchef (Brad Lau)

  48. Worth the detour · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Fragrant Garden

    An authentic family-run Teochew restaurant on Upper Serangoon Road — steamed fish, braised goose and duck, oyster omelette and the mui-and-porridge classics — a fitting anchor for the district's Teochew ('Au Kang') heritage.

    756 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-15/16 Upper Serangoon Shopping Centre, S534626

    Recommended by Dr Leslie Tay (ieatishootipost), Miss Tam Chiak

    Davis Prawn Court

    A roadside Upper Serangoon stall within walking distance of Kovan MRT, packed each morning for handmade Teochew kueh — soon kueh, png kueh — bursting with well-seasoned fillings and made fresh daily.

    1022 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534760

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Singapore Women's Weekly

  51. Worth the detour · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Quan Ji Cooked Food

    A hidden gem at Hainanese Village Centre serving just two dishes — fried Hokkien prawn mee and char kway teow — with almost everything made from scratch: the prawn stock, pork lard, chilli, even hand-peeled garlic. Run by Mrs Lu and her husband for over a decade.

  52. Worth the detour · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Yi Liu Xiang Nasi Lemak

    The First Class Fragrance nasi lemak — by queue, the most popular stall in the whole of Hainanese Village Centre. Fragrant coconut rice with crispy fried fish fillet, ikan selar, whitebait and sambal for a few dollars; regularly sold out before its stated noon close.

    Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-30, Singapore 530105

    Recommended by Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Seth Lui

  53. Worth the detour · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Tachinomiya

    Blk 211 Hougang Street 21, #01-285, Singapore 530211

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Miss Tam Chiak

  58. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Swee Heng Wanton Noodle

    A humble 50-year wanton mee tucked in a back corner of Chomp Chomp (no relation to the bakery of the same name) — springy noodles, silky-skinned wantons and char siew all made in-house, in a broth with robust ikan-bilis notes.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, #01-12, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by Seth Lui, HungryGoWhere, Eatbook.sg

  59. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    5 Star Corner Western Food

    A near-20-year Hougang coffeeshop Western stall famous for huge portions at small prices — chicken chop, sirloin, black-pepper lamb, hot-plate mixed grill and fish & chips. Value old-school hawker Western.

    Blk 805 Hougang Central, #01-116, Singapore 530805

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg, Mothership

  60. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Waa Cow! Yakiniku

    The first yakiniku outlet from the Waa Cow! beef-bowl brand — a grill-it-yourself concept at myVillage with cuts like karubi, oyster blade, striploin and ox tongue plus pork, chicken and veg, from S$4.90.

    myVillage @ Serangoon Garden, 1 Maju Avenue, #02-10/11, Singapore 556679

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui, Mothership

  61. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    myVillage @ Serangoon Gardens

    The neighbourhood mall on the site of the old Serangoon Garden Village and its 1950s Paramount Theatre (demolished 2009). Pitched as a 'village' concept mall, it keeps the Circus area's daily rhythm going with a supermarket, eateries and services.

    Look for Mall hours daily

    1 Maju Avenue, Singapore 556679

    Recommended by Wikipedia, myVillage @ Serangoon Garden

  62. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Montfort Schools (formerly Holy Innocents' English School)

    Founded in 1916 as Holy Innocents' English School beside the Church of the Nativity by the parish priest of Serangoon, renamed Montfort in 1959 and run by the Gabrielite Brothers. A cornerstone of Hougang's 'Holy Land' cluster of Catholic institutions; a heritage gallery traces its founding.

    Look for Active school; grounds not open to visitors

    Montfort Secondary School, 50 Hougang Avenue 8, Singapore 538785

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Roots.gov.sg (NHB)

  63. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Lim Tua Tow Market (heritage site)

    A Hougang Heritage Trail marker recalling Lim Tua Tow market at the old 5th milestone of Upper Serangoon Road — for decades the marketplace that served the population of Singapore's north-eastern region before the town was redeveloped.

    Look for Interpretive heritage marker

    Upper Serangoon Road (former 5th milestone), Kovan, Singapore

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Little Day Out

  64. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Serangoon Stadium & Sport Centre

    The community stadium and adjoining sport centre serving the Serangoon–Hougang belt — running track, stands, gym and pool. A neighbourhood recreation hub on the western edge of the district.

    Look for ActiveSG facility; public sessions & fees apply

    33 Yio Chu Kang Road, Singapore 545677

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NParks (National Parks Board)

  65. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Nex

    The North-East's biggest mall (opened 2011), integrated with Serangoon MRT (NEL/Circle Line interchange) and the air-conditioned bus interchange. The regional shopping-and-transit anchor on the western edge of the Upper Serangoon district, with a rooftop dog run and garden.

    Look for Mall hours daily

    23 Serangoon Central, Singapore 556083

    Recommended by Wikipedia, NParks (National Parks Board)

  66. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Church of St Vincent de Paul

    A Catholic parish on Kovan's western edge whose roots trace to 1959, when Fr Henri Saussard began ministering to the rubber tappers, fishermen and farmers of the Jalan Kayu area; the present church was blessed and opened at Christmas 1970. It continues to serve the north-eastern Catholic community around Serangoon Gardens and Kovan.

    Look for Active parish; Mass times on the church site

    301 Yio Chu Kang Road, Singapore 805910

    Recommended by CATHOLICSG, GCatholic.org

  67. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Holy Innocents' High School

    One of Singapore's first Chinese mission schools, founded in 1892 as Tao Nan School in the Upper Serangoon village and renamed Holy Innocents' Chinese Boys' School in 1920 under Fr Becheras. Part of Hougang's 'Holy Land' cluster of Catholic institutions around the Church of the Nativity; the school returned to a rebuilt Hougang campus, blessed by Archbishop Nicholas Chia in 2006.

    Look for Active school; grounds not open to visitors

    5 Lorong Low Koon, Singapore 536451

    Recommended by Wikipedia, CATHOLICSG

  68. Deep cut · Upper Serangoon

    Zi Yun Kai Ji Gong

    A Taoist temple complex completed in 1996 and a Hougang Heritage Trail 'Architectural Gems' landmark. It houses three older temples — Kai Hock Tong, Keat Sun Beo and Chao Ying Kong — relocated and consolidated from their original sites at Wolskel Road, Lorong Chuan and Yishun, a common Singapore story of temples resettled by redevelopment.

    Look for Active temple; open daytime

    56 Hougang Avenue 3, Singapore 538842

    Recommended by Roots.gov.sg (NHB), Wikipedia

  69. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Chia Keng Fried Hokkien Mee

    The other half of Chomp Chomp's Hokkien mee debate — a darker, wetter plate with its own loyal supporters who rate it over Ah Hock. Between the two, Serangoon Gardens arguably has Singapore's densest Hokkien mee rivalry.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, HungryGoWhere

  70. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Hock Kee Fried Oyster

    A veteran orh luak stall frying crisp, starchy oyster omelettes to order — one of the market's most-named stalls in the food-guide coverage of Serangoon Garden.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui

  71. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Lao Song Fa (Botanical Garden Famous Fishball Noodle)

    An old-name fishball noodle stall carrying the 'Botanical Garden Famous' lineage — springy mee pok tossed with handmade fishballs, fishcake and minced pork, a market staple for decades.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Seth Lui

  72. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Bee Heng Prawn Noodle

    A market prawn-noodle mainstay, its rich prawn-and-pork broth a recurring recommendation in the Serangoon Garden Market guides.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  73. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Fong Kee Delicacies

    An old-school snack stall for hum ji beng, traditional pastries and kueh — the kind of nostalgic bite the Serangoon Garden Market food guides keep flagging.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, Stall 12, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  74. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Pancake King

    A long-standing stall for min jiang kueh (folded peanut pancake) and hum ji beng (from about S$1.30) — a market breakfast and tea-time regular.

    Serangoon Garden Market & Food Centre, #01-25, 49A Serangoon Garden Way, S555945

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Daniel Food Diary

  75. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Bedok North 85 Fried Oyster

    A three-in-one stall doing moist, well-coated Hokkien mee in a velvety prawn stock (about S$3.50), plus fried oyster and white/black carrot cake with eggy bits and preserved radish.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-30, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  76. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Yi Shi Jia Wanton Mee

    A decades-old wanton mee stall with a constant queue for simple, honest bowls of springy noodles in soy sauce with char siew and wantons.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-57, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  77. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    51 Ming Fa Wanton Egg Noodle

    A community-loved wanton mee for its well-charred char siew and springy egg noodles — one of Kovan 209's most cited noodle stalls.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  78. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Yam Mee Teochew Fishball Noodles

    Fishball noodles with a choice of dry, soup or a coconutty, mildly spicy laksa broth, topped with fishcake, minced meat and braised mushroom — a Kovan 209 regular.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  79. Deep cut · Indian & Roti Prata · Upper Serangoon

    Srisun Express

    A 24-hour prata house that gave R.K. its cross-street rival — prata, murtabak and maggi goreng served with massive drink towers, a Serangoon Gardens supper staple.

    56 Serangoon Garden Way, S555952

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, The Honeycombers

  80. Deep cut · Indian & Roti Prata · Upper Serangoon

    Al-Falah

    The mainstay 24/7 mamak for Kovan and Hougang residents — plain prata about S$2.60 for two, egg prata, murtabak and teh tarik at any hour. A Hougang-edge supper anchor.

    Hougang Village, 681 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-855, S530681

    Recommended by ladyironchef (Brad Lau), City Nomads (Singapore city guide)

  81. Deep cut · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Wang Da Shen Chicken Wing & Satay

    One of Chomp Chomp's newer stalls (opened during the pandemic) and the only one that stays open till 2am — charcoal-grilled chicken wings and satay for the deep-supper crowd at Serangoon Gardens.

    Chomp Chomp Food Centre, 20 Kensington Park Road, S557269

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Eatbook.sg

  82. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Fa Ji Minced Meat Fishball Noodle

    The most popular of Kovan 209's three fishball-noodle stalls — springy noodles tossed with handmade fishballs, fishcake and minced pork, a heartland breakfast regular.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-05, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Seth Lui, Her World Singapore

  83. Deep cut · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Hajjah Mariam Muslim Food

    Kovan 209's go-to Malay-Muslim stall — nasi lemak sets alongside hawker staples like mee rebus, mee siam, lontong and soto, the halal anchor of the food centre.

    Kovan 209 Market & Food Centre, #01-53, 209 Hougang Street 21, S530209

    Recommended by Her World Singapore, Seth Lui

  84. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Two Cranes

    A minimalist neighbourhood cafe in Kovan serving a focused menu of Korean-leaning fusion food, bingsu desserts and hand-crafted beverages — a modern counterpoint to the estate's old-school stalls.

    Block 211 Hougang Street 21, #01-291, S530211

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, Eatbook.sg

  85. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Dessert Bowl

    A Serangoon Gardens dessert institution on the second floor of a shophouse — famous for its trademarked durian mousse served on ice with a dollop of durian flesh, one of 50-plus traditional Chinese desserts.

    80A Serangoon Garden Way, Singapore

    Recommended by TheSmartLocal, Time Out Singapore

  86. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Ng Kuan Chilli Pan Mee

    A KL-style chilli ban mian in an Upper Serangoon Road coffee shop, open into the small hours — al-dente noodles with minced pork, ikan bilis, fried shallots, a runny egg and a fierce dried-shrimp chilli that draws the supper crowd.

    943 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  87. Deep cut · Wok Noodles (Char Kway Teow, Hokkien Mee, Bak Chor Mee) · Upper Serangoon

    Yi Ji Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee

    A popular Kovan fried Hokkien prawn mee that has spawned several branches — a spicy, prawn-rich plate with meat and abalone. The Upper Serangoon original anchors the group.

    965 Upper Serangoon Road (Mee Sek Food Court), Singapore 534721

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui

  88. Deep cut · Chinese, Dim Sum & Teochew · Upper Serangoon

    Yi Dian Xin Hong Kong Dim Sum

    An affordable Upper Serangoon dim sum spot near Kovan doing hearty Hong Kong-style plates — signature prawn dumplings and salted-egg custard bao among them. A neighbourhood dim sum fix.

    973 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534725

    Recommended by AsiaOne, Miss Tam Chiak

  89. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    88 Pocha

    A pojangmacha-style Korean tent-bar in Kovan — Korean fried chicken, army stew and soju into the small hours. A late-night Korean option on Upper Serangoon Road.

    957 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534717

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Daniel Food Diary

  90. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Goldhill Family Restaurant

    A long-running Hougang cai png shop beloved for very affordable economic rice — fried chicken wings, braised pork, stir-fried veg — from as little as S$2 a plate.

    Blk 6 Hougang Avenue 3, #01-78, Singapore 530006

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Eatbook.sg

  91. Deep cut · Bak Kut Teh & Soups · Upper Serangoon

    Mei Xi Hakka Yong Tau Foo

    A Ci Yuan stall where the Hakka owner marinates her own fish paste and offers unusual items — fried bean rolls, deep-fried yam strings and egg rolls — alongside the usual yong tau foo pieces.

    Ci Yuan Hawker Centre, 51 Hougang Avenue 9, #01-17, Singapore 538776

    Recommended by Miss Tam Chiak, Seth Lui

  92. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    The Larder Cafe

    A Serangoon Gardens brunch cafe (second outlet after Toa Payoh) celebrated for its egg dishes, mains and desserts in an easy neighbourhood setting.

    66A Serangoon Garden Way, Singapore 555962

    Recommended by ladyironchef (Brad Lau), Daniel Food Diary

  93. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Picky Snout

    A Western coffeeshop stall hidden in a Kovan kopitiam eight minutes from the MRT, doing generous rosti with oversized pork chops and chargrilled chicken chops at affordable prices.

    1014 Upper Serangoon Road, Singapore 534752

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  94. Deep cut · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Fatto Catto

    A Simon Road matcha-specialty cafe near Kovan by the team behind Fat Cat Ice Cream Bar — premium Japanese matcha, creative tea drinks, artisan ice cream and a matcha Basque burnt cheesecake that often sells out within hours.

    15 Simon Road, Singapore 545903

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, HungryGoWhere

  95. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Kovan Scrambled Egg Rice

    A cult scrambled-egg-rice stall (高文滑蛋饭) — silky wat-dan-style egg over rice — that outgrew its old Kovan 209 home and relocated to a Hougang Avenue 7 coffeeshop in mid-2024.

    Blk 335 Hougang Avenue 7, Singapore 530335

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  96. Deep cut · Hawker & Zi Char · Upper Serangoon

    Dong Jin Yuan Dian Xin

    A 40-year-old Hainanese Village Centre stall, now run by second-gen hawker Nicholas Neo, famous for finger-sized fried carrot cake sticks — crisp outside, tender inside — sold by the thousand daily.

    Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-04, Singapore 530105

    Recommended by Johor Kaki (Tony Boey), Her World Singapore

  97. Deep cut · Malay & Nasi Padang · Upper Serangoon

    Roasted Pork Belly Nasi Lemak

    A Hainanese Village Centre stall (easy to spot by its fuchsia signboard) plating fragrant coconut rice with crackly-skinned roasted pork belly and crispy ikan bilis — S$3 sets that draw an early crowd.

    Hainanese Village Centre, 105 Hougang Avenue 1, #02-28, Singapore 530105

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, Seth Lui

  98. Deep cut · Chendol, Kueh & Durian · Upper Serangoon

    Happy Oven

    A family-run old-school bakery in Hougang turning out traditional S$1 cakes and pastries — pandan, kaya, sugar rolls — the kind of heartland bakery that's getting rarer.

    678 Hougang Avenue 8, #01-505, Singapore 530678

    Recommended by Eatbook.sg, HungryGoWhere

  99. Closed — kept for the record · Cafés & Modern · Upper Serangoon

    Amber Ember — CLOSED

    A well-loved Kovan brunch cafe for specialty coffee and toasted jaffles in a light, plant-filled space — it closed on 19 Jan 2025. Kept here as a flagged closure.

    730 Upper Serangoon Road, #01-01, Singapore

    Recommended by Daniel Food Diary, City Nomads (Singapore city guide)
